newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors demand jail for Hanbo founder.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors demand jail for Hanbo founder.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Monday demanded a 20-year jail sentence for the founder of the Hanbo Group, Chung Tae-soo, who is at the centre of a corruption scandal that has rocked the nation.
At a court hearing, prosecutors also called for a six-year prison sentence for Chung's son, Chung Bo-keun, the chairman of Hanbo. Both men have been charged with bribery and embezzlement.

The father and son are among 11 people on trial for corruption in connection with the failure of Hanbo's steelmaking flagship in January under debts of five trillion won, allegedly extracted with bribes.

Prosecutors also demanded a six-year jail term for former Home Affairs minister Kim Woo-suk; 7-1/2 years for ruling New Korea Party lawmaker Hong In-gil; five years each for two other ruling party lawmakers, Hwang Byung-tai and Chung Jae-chull; and seven years for Kwon Roh-kap, a prominent lawmaker with the main opposition National Congress for New Politics.

They also asked for seven years each for the former president of Korea First Bank, Sheen Kwang-shik, and the former head of the Chohung Bank, Woo Chan-mok. They demanded eight years for another former Korean First president, Rhee Chul-soo.
In addition, prosecutors asked the Seoul District Criminal Court to jail for five years the former financial controller of the Hanbo Group, Kim Jong-kook.
